intended_object: A dummy bound variable used inside a machine-generated nominal proof certificate ("nb095_alpha_dummy_452"). It picks a variable that is fresh for the free variables of two earlier auxiliary class terms. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
I judged this from the definition, its docstring and its name. I did not open the definitions it calls (`freshVar`, `Class.cv`, `nb095AlphaDummy447`, `nb095AlphaDummy448`), since the verdict does not depend on what they compute.

The body only chooses a fresh variable, `freshVar (... ∪ ...) 0`, so that it avoids the free variables of two other auxiliary terms, `nb095AlphaDummy447 f` and `nb095AlphaDummy448 f`. This is renaming bookkeeping for alpha-conversion inside an auto-generated proof certificate. The docstring says so directly: "Checked nominal proof certificate".

It has no counterpart in the mathematical literature. It is an implementation detail of the library's syntactic proof machinery, so there is nothing in Mathlib to compare it with.
